originalQuestion: Why did a category tied for third disappear from the returns ranking?
clarifiedQuestion: For items returned in December 2025 UTC, list the categories with the three highest distinct return counts. Include every category tied at a qualifying count.
humanResponse:
Rank the category counts with DENSE_RANK. Use the category name only to order the final display so tied counts receive the same rank.

```sql
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) AS returned_items
  FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS i
  JOIN `tv_thelook.products` AS p ON p.id = i.product_id
  WHERE i.returned_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00 UTC'
    AND i.returned_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC'
  GROUP BY p.category
)
SELECT category, returned_items, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY returned_items DESC) AS count_rank
FROM counts
QUALIFY count_rank <= 3
ORDER BY returned_items DESC, category ASC
LIMIT 9999
```
